architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

core_scientific_tool.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
core_scientific_tool.role: Convert the paper's upstream findings into machine-usable design rules without exposing the validation formulation or its outcome.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities
reproducibility of the recommendation under the same evidence contract
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

acceptance_criterion.claim: A frozen preparation and measurement protocol can produce an E2 reactive-core baseline reproducible enough to support a later modifier-performance comparison.
acceptance_criterion.criterion: For at least three independently prepared S1C02 realizations, obtain complete matched 80-130 °C rheology and 120 °C hold measurements at 15, 30, 60, and 90 min. The probe passes only if the consistently timed 120 °C state-anchor viscosity has sample CV below 0.46 and max/min ratio below 2.8, both stricter than the lower bounds of the historical E2 dispersion, while all preparations remain homogeneous and free of phase separation, gelation, skinning, nonuniform sampling, or loading inconsistency. Report each run's starting viscosity, absolute viscosity changes, SI15-60, and SI15-90 without converting them into a modifier-performance claim.
acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: If either repeatability limit is not met, any required measurement is missing, process histories differ, or a processability failure occurs, process/realization uncertainty remains unresolved and no acrylic-plus-tackifier performance candidate may be adjudicated from a nominal viscosity comparison.
acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: Full temperature response within 80-130 °C plus a matched 120 °C hold at 15, 30, 60, and 90 min

alternatives_considered.relative_reason: Preferred subsequent performance-mitigation candidate because 15 wt% AC1920 and 5 wt% TK100 cover both supported axes and place the tackifier dose in the repeatedly documented minor-resin region. It is deferred until modifier specifications, reactive-equivalent balance, process history, and the contemporaneous E2 baseline are resolved.

Not selected as the default performance experiment because its 2.5 wt% TK100 dose is below the supplied 3-10 wt% broad supported region, its minimum-sufficient status is unproven, and the fine-grid provenance is not fully auditable. It would be interpretable only as a lower-dose uncertainty probe after material and stoichiometric verification.

Covers both intervention axes with lower total burden, but 10 wt% acrylic lies below the principal 15-25 wt% analogue-supported region, making a null result ambiguous between inadequate dose and failure of the formulation-family hypothesis.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: Failure mode first: local experiments establish a formulation-dependent viscosity rise during a 120 °C hold, with E1 showing SI15-60 about 0.095 and SI15-90 about 0.168 and E5 showing about 0.515 and 0.931. They also show unusually large E2 run dispersion, so nominal viscosity cannot be treated as a state-independent formulation property. Experiment intent is nominally performance mitigation, which would ordinarily require both independently supported modifier axes. However, an interpretable performance experiment is presently blocked by unknown AC1920/TK100 solids, moisture, reactive functionality, compatibility, true NCO:OH, and missing process history; therefore this decision explicitly substitutes a partial-coverage process-state control for the full mitigation experiment. The paper-derived rheological rules used here are that realization state mainly shifts viscosity level within the audited local family, that a consistently timed state anchor is required, and that thermal-hold stability must be measured over the matched hold window rather than inferred from static viscosity. Curated PUR literature/database priors support an acrylic-like region around 15-25 wt% and a minor tackifier region around 3-10 wt%, repeatedly near 5 wt%; these priors identify S1C41 as the eventual bounded dual-axis performance candidate but are not treated as predictors of its wet-lab outcome. Conservative experimental-design constraints introduced here are at least three independent preparations, frozen process history, a contemporaneous S1C02 hold baseline, and repeatability limits referenced to the observed historical E2 dispersion. This resolves the Skeptic and Robustness-Adjudicator objections: S1C40 is not promoted by minimum modifier burden because its 2.5 wt% tackifier dose has unproven sufficiency and uncertain refinement provenance; S1C41 is deferred rather than rejected and becomes the preferred performance test after the required material, stoichiometric, and process controls pass. Exact analogue distance is not used as an objective, and no exact property prediction is made.

evidence_coverage.note: S1C02 is a no-intervention baseline control. It is sufficient for process-state uncertainty resolution but not for testing the acrylic-plus-minor-tackifier mitigation hypothesis.

extrapolation.note: S1C02 exactly reproduces the measured E2 reactive-core composition and remains inside the measured 80-130 °C domain; no modifier-family extrapolation is made.

measurement.note: Instrument-level measurement uncertainty and an uncertainty-interval method were not supplied; raw viscosity, absolute change, fractional drift, and run-level results must be retained.

process_history.note: Six major process-history fields are absent from the candidate record, so process freezing is mandatory.

repeatability.note: Historical E2 sample CV was approximately 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratio approximately 2.8-3.6. The probe tests whether a frozen process reduces this realization-state dispersion.

action_requests.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
action_requests.reason: Required first bridge from the upstream physical analysis. It will establish whether formulation-only or state-aware description is supported, whether one-point state calibration is effective, and which temperature and hold responses must govern candidate selection.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Retrieve the measured lower-drift 120 °C trajectory and deterministic descriptors as the directly commensurate local stability reference.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Retrieve the measured high-drift 120 °C trajectory and deterministic descriptors defining the local failure severity to be mitigated.

action_requests.name: get_repeatability_risk
action_requests.reason: Quantify realization-state risk for the reactive-core anchor before treating its nominal viscosity as a formulation property or ranking modifier candidates against it.

action_requests.name: get_temperature_support
action_requests.reason: Confirm the supported temperature interval and identify an in-domain anchor temperature for one-point state calibration and candidate comparison.

action_requests.name: inspect_formulation
action_requests.reason: Establish the original reactive-core composition, MDI fraction, and stoichiometric basis before interpreting candidate modifier fractions or dilution of reactive components.

action_requests.name: inspect_formulation
action_requests.reason: Identify the composition of the lower-drift local reference so that its hold behavior is not conflated with an undocumented chemistry or process-state difference.

action_requests.name: inspect_formulation
action_requests.reason: Identify the composition of the high-drift local reference and determine which formulation differences can legitimately inform the mitigation objective without asserting causality.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: After establishing the local objective, retrieve the candidate-to-composition mapping, E2 anchor, independent modifier axes, and claim boundary needed to compare candidate regions without using held-out information.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Absolute and fractional viscosity drift over the directly supported 120 °C, 15-60 min and 15-90 min hold intervals
Initial hold viscosity at 15 min, kept separate from subsequent drift
Viscosity level at an in-domain calibration temperature
State-calibrated viscosity level if supported by the master-curve analysis
Apparent temperature-response coordinate over measured support
Repeat/run dispersion under independently prepared realizations
Acrylic-like fraction relative to the broad 15-25 wt% analogue-supported region
Tackifier-like fraction within the conservative 0-10 wt% region
Combined-modifier loading and distance from the E2 reactive-core-only counterfactual
MDI fraction, reactive-equivalent balance, and uncertainty in modifier functionality or OH contribution
Processability during preparation and hold, including homogeneity and absence of phase separation or gelation
Sensitivity to moisture, aging, mixing, loading, and thermal history
Extrapolation distance from local compositions and from directly supported literature regions
Evidence type for each design choice: directly commensurate local measurement, directional/noncommensurate external evidence, or conservative extrapolation-control principle
counterfactual_checks: Compare the selected intervention with the E2 reactive-core-only option under the same process and measurement schedule.
Check whether any apparent reduction in percentage drift is merely caused by a higher 15 min starting viscosity by reviewing both absolute and fractional changes.
Check whether matching one viscosity point still leaves a different temperature-response slope, indicating that a level shift alone is insufficient.
Check whether state calibration collapses preparation-to-preparation offsets; if it does not, process realization remains unresolved.
Check whether the candidate's benefit persists through 90 min rather than appearing only at an early hold point.
Check whether the selected point remains within independently supported acrylic and tackifier bounds and was not chosen by converting a directional literature percentage into an exact optimum.
Check whether a change in MDI fraction or reactive-equivalent balance could explain the result instead of modifier identity.

Check whether a single-axis bounded candidate would provide similar expected mitigation with lower stoichiometric or process uncertainty; retain the combined intervention only if both axes contribute defensible performance value.
Check the result against both E1 and E5: improvement over E5 alone is insufficient if the candidate remains substantially less stable than the attainable E1 reference.
Do not use the blinded validation formulation identity or any later outcome in candidate selection or interpretation.
planner.decision_goal: Select one bounded, evidence-supported candidate experiment that mitigates the locally observed 120 °C hot-hold viscosity drift while retaining a usable viscosity level and temperature response, with process/state calibration sufficient to distinguish a formulation effect from realization variability.
design_implications: Optimize hot-hold stability as an independent response rather than optimizing only viscosity at one temperature.
Use the canonical state-aware rheology result to determine whether a one-point state calibration is required before comparing candidate viscosity levels or temperature-response coordinates.
Keep candidate evaluation within the measured 80-130 °C temperature domain and use 120 °C as the directly supported hold temperature unless new domain evidence is generated.
Compare the candidate against the original E1 and E5 hold trajectories using the same schedule and SI definition; E1 is the lower-drift local reference and E5 is the high-drift failure reference.

A multi-component acrylic-plus-tackifier intervention is admissible in performance-mitigation mode because both modifier axes have independent external support, provided each remains within its bounded evidence-supported region and reactive-core stoichiometry is checked.
Treat approximately 15-25 wt% acrylic and no more than approximately 10 wt% tackifier as broad analogue-supported search regions, not exact total-formulation optima.
Preserve a reactive-core-only option as a counterfactual, but do not default to single-axis isolation because the stated objective is mitigation rather than causal attribution.
Record mixing, drying, reaction, aging, loading, and thermal history because the observed run spread indicates that process state may dominate a nominal viscosity comparison.
Do not attribute hot-hold drift to a molecular mechanism from rheology alone; modifier loading, functionality, stoichiometry, moisture, and process history remain competing explanations.
material_regularities_to_use: Across measured temperature sweeps, viscosity decreases monotonically from 80 to 130 °C and individual runs are described well by Andrade-type temperature dependence.

E2 exhibits large nominal repeat/run spread at every measured temperature: sample CV is approximately 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratio approximately 2.8-3.6, so a single nominal viscosity must not be treated as a state-independent material property.
Thermal response and temporal hot-hold response are distinct: temperature sweeps characterize reversible temperature dependence over 80-130 °C, whereas 120 °C holds reveal time-dependent drift.
The original hold data show a direct local stability contrast: E1 has SI15-60 about 0.095 and SI15-90 about 0.168, while E5 has SI15-60 about 0.515 and SI15-90 about 0.931.
The E2 reactive core is the declared anchor for the prospective candidate lattice; acrylic-like loading and tackifier-like loading are independent candidate axes.

External acrylic and tackifier records are formulation-family priors rather than local optima. Acrylic analogues support coarse regions around 15-25 wt%, while tackifier guidance supports a minor axis up to about 10 wt%.

The external 25 wt% low-OH versus higher-OH acrylic comparison is directional evidence that modifier functionality may affect stability; it does not establish the mechanism or predict the local candidate exactly.
The external long-duration stability criterion of about 25% rise over 4-10 h is noncommensurate with the local 15-90 min hold and must not be used as a local numerical pass threshold.
planner.physical_failure_mode: The primary established failure mode is time-dependent viscosity increase during a 120 °C hold, with a strong contrast between original formulations E1 and E5. Nominal viscosity alone is not an adequate objective because E2 also shows large run-to-run level variation, indicating that realization or process state can shift measured viscosity independently of formulation identity.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: A frozen pre-result formulation and process record, including component masses, lot identities, modifier solids basis, MDI amount, assumed OH/NCO contributions, drying, mixing, reaction, aging, loading, and thermal history
At least one viscosity measurement at the state-calibration temperature selected from the measured 80-130 °C support before interpreting the full temperature response
A temperature sweep within 80-130 °C using the same protocol as the original data to estimate viscosity level and apparent temperature sensitivity
A 120 °C hold trajectory at the original 15, 30, 60, and 90 min time points
Pre-specified SI15-60 and SI15-90 calculations using SI=(eta_t1-eta_t0)/eta_t0, with source viscosity units preserved rather than invented
Direct comparison with E1 and E5 using identical hold timing and thermal protocol
Independent preparation or run replication sufficient to assess whether candidate improvement exceeds the large realization spread observed for E2
Process observations for mixing behavior, homogeneity, phase separation, skinning, gelation, and instrument-loading consistency
Reactive-equivalent and mass-balance verification after modifier addition so that apparent stability improvement is not accepted when caused by an unintended stoichiometric shift
uncertainty_triggers: If the state-aware summary does not support transferable one-point calibration, require replicated full sweeps rather than correcting candidates with a single viscosity value.
If candidate run spread is comparable to E2's approximately 0.46-0.58 CV or approximately 2.8-3.6 max/min ratio, classify the result as uncertainty resolution rather than formulation improvement.
If the candidate falls outside 80-130 °C measurement support or outside the 15-90 min hold window, classify conclusions for the new domain as unsupported until measured.
If modifier functionality, solids content, OH value, or compatibility is unknown, do not interpret loading percentage alone as the active variable.
If MDI or reactive-equivalent balance changes materially relative to E2, treat stoichiometry as a confounder and require a matched control or reformulation.
If the preparation or thermal history differs from the original references, do not attribute a viscosity or drift difference solely to chemistry.
If the candidate shows acceptable initial viscosity but substantial positive hold drift, reject nominal-viscosity-only success.
If phase separation, gelation, or nonuniform sampling occurs, classify rheological comparison as out of domain or process-confounded.
If evidence is used beyond the broad 15-25 wt% acrylic or 0-10 wt% tackifier regions, require an explicit extrapolation rationale rather than treating the external records as direct anchors.
If acrylic and tackifier are combined and performance changes, do not infer which modifier caused the change without a later causal-isolation experiment.

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: The candidate mitigates the locally observed 120 °C hot-hold viscosity drift without the conclusion being explained solely by a shifted starting viscosity or uncontrolled realization state.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.criterion: Across independent preparations, both mean SI15-60 and mean SI15-90 must be closer to the E1 references than to the E5 references, corresponding to SI15-60 < 0.305 and SI15-90 < 0.550, and the replicate uncertainty interval must exclude the respective E5 value. Absolute viscosity changes must show the same conclusion, the improvement must persist through 90 min, and no phase separation, gelation, or nonuniform sampling may occur. Initial viscosity and the 80-130 °C response must be reported separately rather than used as substitutes for hold stability.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Reject or classify as unresolved if either stability index is not improved toward E1, if apparent fractional improvement is caused only by a higher 15 min viscosity, if run dispersion is comparable to the historical E2 variability and overlaps the E5 response, if the temperature-response shape cannot be calibrated, or if stoichiometric/process confounding, phase separation, or gelation occurs.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: 120 °C from 15 to 90 min, with primary comparisons at 15-60 and 15-90 min

provisional_measurement_plan.primary_response: Replicated absolute viscosity change and fractional stability indices SI15-60 and SI15-90 during a matched 120 °C hold; report the 15 min starting viscosity separately.
provisional_measurement_plan.state_anchor_plan: Use independently prepared replicates with frozen drying, mixing, reaction, aging, loading, and thermal histories. Obtain a 120 °C state-specific viscosity anchor for each realization. On at least the first realization, perform the full matched 80-130 °C sweep to verify that the resin-modified candidate retains the local shared thermal-response shape; use one-point level calibration for later realizations only if this transfer is confirmed. Run S1C02 and, where feasible, E1 and E5 references under the same schedule.
provisional_measurement_plan.time_window: 15, 30, 60, and 90 min, with pre-specified SI15-60 and SI15-90

evidence_against: The local measurements do not establish that either modifier reduces hold drift; that expectation is an external formulation-family prior.
The 15 wt% acrylic evidence is directional/noncommensurate rather than an exact total-formulation numeric anchor.
The 2.5 wt% tackifier level is below the directly commensurate 4.8-6.4 wt% examples, so support is for the minor-tackifier direction rather than this exact loading.
All major process-history fields are missing, and the state-shift model was established only within the original local chemistry family.

The deterministic sufficiency diagnostic classifies it as full coverage with no unsupported active axis and strong analogue-region support.
It preserves the relative E2 reactive-core proportions, allowing comparison with the E2 reactive-core-only counterfactual while changing the bounded modifier axes.
Local diagnosis supplies the response objective and need for state control; external formulation knowledge supplies the acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like intervention directions.
Among strong-support, full-coverage candidates, it has the lowest total modifier burden at 17.5 wt%, making it the minimum sufficient perturbation under the supplied diagnostics.
key_uncertainty: AC1920 and TK100 functionality, solids basis, OH contribution, moisture, and compatibility are not supplied.
True NCO:OH balance after modifier addition is unresolved.
It is unknown whether the local shared thermal-response shape transfers to this resin-modified chemistry.
Potential phase separation, gelation, or preparation sensitivity could confound the hold response.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: It directly interrogates the measured failure mode with complete intervention-axis coverage while minimizing modifier burden among strongly supported full-coverage candidates. A matched 120 °C hold can falsify the mitigation hypothesis without treating literature proximity as an outcome predictor.

evidence_against: Its 20 wt% combined modifier burden is greater than S1C40, so it is not the minimum perturbation.
The 15 wt% acrylic anchor remains directional/noncommensurate.
Directly commensurate tackifier proximity does not imply better local performance and is not used as the primary ranking objective.
No local resin-modified hold measurements establish transferability.

It tests whether the minor tackifier direction remains useful at the repeatedly documented loading while directly measuring the local 120 °C drift response.
It retains the E2 reactive-core proportions, so differences can be interpreted against an E2-based matched control subject to stoichiometric verification.
key_uncertainty: Whether increasing TK100 from 2.5 to 5 wt% improves drift or only changes initial viscosity.
Whether reactive-equivalent balance changes because of modifier functionality.
Whether independent preparations exhibit dispersion comparable to the high E2 run spread.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: It is a strong follow-on or parallel robustness point because it places the tackifier axis in the directly commensurate external cluster while retaining full intervention coverage. Comparison with S1C40 would test sensitivity to the minor-axis dose without changing the acrylic level.

evidence_against: Its analogue support is only moderate, and 10 wt% acrylic lies below the broad 15-25 wt% acrylic region emphasized by the external evidence.
The 2.5 wt% tackifier level is below the directly commensurate 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster.
Lower modifier burden cannot compensate for weaker evidence support; therefore it ranks below strongly supported full-coverage candidates.
evidence_for: It is the lowest-burden full-coverage candidate, containing 10 wt% AC1920 and 2.5 wt% TK100 for 12.5 wt% total modifier.
It preserves the E2 core proportions and directly tests the same 120 °C drift failure rather than relying on static viscosity.
The deterministic diagnostics classify both supported axes as covered, making it preferable to a zero-axis candidate when testing performance mitigation.
key_uncertainty: Whether this lower-bound intervention is sufficient to produce a hold-drift change larger than realization variability.
Whether a null result would reflect insufficient loading rather than failure of the modifier-family hypothesis.
Whether the state-aware thermal model remains applicable after modification.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: It resolves whether meaningful mitigation is possible below the main acrylic analogue region. It is informative as a lower-bound full-coverage probe, but it is not the default performance choice because its acrylic loading has weaker external support.

evidence_against: It covers neither independently supported modifier axis and therefore is not a sufficient performance-mitigation candidate.
A baseline control does not test the combined resin-modification hypothesis.
E2 already exhibits substantial realization-state variability, so a single control run would be inadequate.
evidence_for: It is the measured E2 reactive-core composition and provides the clean matched counterfactual requested by the Planner.
It preserves the locally characterized NCO:OH = 1.80, 50/50 polyol core without resin modifiers.
Running it under the identical preparation, calibration, sweep, and hold schedule helps determine whether an apparent improvement is formulation-related or caused by process state.
key_uncertainty: The E2 hold trajectory is not supplied.
Its large historical run spread may obscure candidate-control differences unless independent preparations are replicated.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: It is an essential mechanistic and process control, not a rank-1 performance intervention. A matched E2 hold establishes the contemporaneous baseline needed to distinguish modifier effects from realization-state shifts.

regularities_used: Measured local evidence: E5 defines the severe hot-hold failure, with SI15-60 = 0.515 and SI15-90 = 0.931; E1 is the lower-drift local reference, with SI15-60 = 0.095 and SI15-90 = 0.168.

Measured local evidence: E2 has large run-to-run viscosity dispersion across 80-130 °C, with CV approximately 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratio approximately 2.8-3.6, so nominal viscosity is strongly realization-state dependent.

Derived physical/model rule: within the audited local chemistry, realization state predominantly shifts viscosity level while a common thermal-response shape is retained; one-point calibration gave roughly 6-10% multiplicative error, but transfer to resin-modified chemistry must be verified.
Derived design rule: static viscosity and 120 °C temporal drift are separate responses; mitigation must therefore be adjudicated from a matched 15-90 min hold rather than a single viscosity value.

External analogue evidence: acrylic-modified PUR formulations support a broad acrylic-like region near 15-25 wt%; approximately 19-20 wt% and 25 wt% are directly commensurate total-formulation numeric anchors, whereas the reported 15% level is directional because its denominator is not fully verified.
External analogue evidence: tackifier-like PUR examples provide directly commensurate numeric anchors around 4.8-6.4 wt%, with broader directional guidance below about 10 wt%.
External directional evidence: acrylic functionality may affect hold stability, but it does not establish a local mechanism or predict AC1920 performance.

Conservative design principle: for performance mitigation, compare candidates covering both independently supported axes before partial-coverage controls, then prefer the minimum sufficient modifier burden within a scientifically supported class.

Diagnostic limitation: intervention-coverage and analogue-support classifications identify interpretable candidate families; they are not rheological property predictions, and exact distance to literature percentages is audit metadata only.
proposer.scientific_target: Mitigate the measured time-dependent viscosity increase during a 120 °C hold while preserving a usable, monotonic 80-130 °C rheological response and separating formulation effects from realization-state variability.
unresolved_questions: What are the verified OH values, reactive functionality, solids contents, and moisture specifications of AC1920 and TK100?
Does modifier addition preserve the intended reactive-equivalent balance, or must MDI be adjusted to maintain a matched NCO:OH basis?
Does the shared state-shift thermal model transfer from the original local chemistry to acrylic/tackifier-modified formulations?
How many independent preparations are required to separate a candidate effect from the historical E2 CV of approximately 0.46-0.58?
What operational viscosity range defines usable processing under the intended application?
Are AC1920 and TK100 homogeneous and stable under the specified preparation and 120 °C hold conditions?

Evidence supports a bounded formulation family rather than an exact composition; the selected 15 wt% acrylic and 2.5 wt% tackifier point is a minimum-burden test within that family, not a predicted optimum.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: It preserves full dual-axis coverage and places TK100 at the directly documented 5 wt% minor-resin level, with only a modest increase in total modifier burden from 17.5 to 20 wt%.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: A performance-mitigation experiment is pursued after material specifications and reactive-equivalent balance are verified.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: It minimizes perturbation but a null result cannot distinguish failure of the tackifier direction from inadequate tackifier dose.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The 2.5 wt% tackifier level receives a documented conservative-extrapolation rationale and the experiment is explicitly labeled a lower-dose uncertainty probe rather than a minimum-sufficient performance test.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: It retains both axes at 12.5 wt% total modifier but has weaker acrylic-region support, making a null result ambiguous.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The objective changes to probing whether mitigation is possible below the principal acrylic-supported region with minimal total modifier.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: It is the essential contemporaneous reactive-core control but does not test either supported modifier intervention axis.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The immediate objective changes from performance mitigation to resolving process-state or stoichiometric uncertainty.

required_conditions: Verify and freeze AC1920 and TK100 lot identity, solids basis, OH value or other NCO-reactive functionality, moisture specification, and compatibility information.
Recalculate true NCO:OH and mass balance after modifier addition; preserve a specified reactive-equivalent basis or include a stoichiometrically matched control.
Use S1C41 rather than S1C40 for the subsequent performance test unless 2.5 wt% TK100 is explicitly justified and treated as a lower-dose uncertainty probe.
Make independently prepared, contemporaneous S1C02 controls mandatory under the identical preparation, state-anchor, sweep, and hold schedule.
Freeze drying, mixing, reaction, aging, loading, and thermal histories before testing.
Specify independent-preparation count, uncertainty-interval method and confidence level, and the rule for determining whether dispersion is comparable to historical E2 variability.
Define quantitative limits for usable initial viscosity, absolute viscosity change, and acceptable thermal-response-shape or prediction error.
Predefine state-anchor timing and require replicated full 80-130 °C sweeps if the modified chemistry fails the frozen transfer criterion.
Treat the E1/E5 midpoint SI thresholds as provisional reconstructed decision rules and account for uncertainty in the single-run E1 and E5 references.
Document the provenance of the 2.5 wt% refinement before using S1C40 in any prospective ranking claim.

robustness_checks.detail: S1C40 directly tests mitigation of 120 °C viscosity drift through matched SI15-60 and SI15-90 measurements rather than relying on nominal viscosity alone.
The Planner declares performance_mitigation, and S1C40 activates both independently supported axes. A single-axis candidate would be a mechanistic control rather than the default performance test.

robustness_checks.check: Supported-region robustness without exact analogue-distance rewards
robustness_checks.detail: S1C40 uses 2.5 wt% TK100, below the stated 3-10 wt% broad tackifier region and the repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster. Treating evidence as a supported region therefore favors S1C41 at 15 wt% acrylic plus 5 wt% tackifier.

S1C40 was promoted because it is the lowest-burden candidate labeled strong-support/full-coverage, but sufficiency of its below-region tackifier dose is not established. Modifier burden cannot override individual-axis support.
S1C40 remains directionally relevant, but its rank is unstable if direct tackifier examples are weighted more strongly than general minor-axis guidance. S1C41 is less dependent on that weighting.
AC1920 and TK100 solids, OH or other NCO-reactive functionality, moisture, compatibility, and resulting true NCO:OH are unresolved, while all major process-history fields are missing.

Rank 1 depends on the unsupported classification of 2.5 wt% tackifier as a sufficient evidence-covered intervention and on an unverified minimum-sufficient-dose assumption, not merely on a robust supported-region rule.

The hold schedule, separate starting-viscosity reporting, full-sweep verification, and absolute plus fractional drift measurements are appropriate. However, replicated S1C02 is optional, replicate count and interval method are unspecified, usable-viscosity and absolute-drift limits are undefined, and no frozen thermal-shape-transfer criterion is provided.

One-point calibration is supported only within the original chemistry family. It remains usable only after a predefined full-sweep transfer test on the modified chemistry; otherwise replicated full sweeps are required.

No held-out result is disclosed, but the 2.5 wt% fine-grid level was formalized after the validation experiment and lacks a repository freeze artifact, so its prospective provenance requires documentation.
The Skeptic identified high-severity dose-support, stoichiometric, and process-state issues sufficient to prevent acceptance of S1C40 as the default performance candidate.

counterfactual_failures: The E2 reactive-core-only counterfactual is described as being run only where feasible rather than as a required matched control.
The proposal does not specify how changes in MDI fraction or true reactive-equivalent balance will be separated from modifier effects if either modifier is NCO-reactive.
The E1 and E5 midpoint criterion does not account for uncertainty in those single-run reference trajectories.
No frozen rule states when failure of thermal-shape transfer invalidates one-point state calibration and triggers replicated full sweeps.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C40 was selected because it is the lowest-burden candidate classified as strong-support/full-coverage, but there are no local resin-modified hold measurements showing that 15 wt% acrylic plus 2.5 wt% tackifier is sufficient. The proposer itself states that local measurements do not establish that either modifier reduces hold drift.
critical_findings.issue: The rank-1 point applies a minimum-sufficient-intervention rule before sufficiency is established.

critical_findings.evidence: The candidate hypothesis defines a broad tackifier-supported region of 3-10 wt% and a repeated directly commensurate cluster of 4.8-6.4 wt%. S1C40 contains 2.5 wt% TK100. Independent support for a tackifier axis does not by itself establish this below-region loading as an evidence-supported full intervention.
critical_findings.issue: The evidence classification for the 2.5 wt% tackifier dose is not consistent with the supplied evidence bounds.

critical_findings.evidence: AC1920 and TK100 functionality, OH contribution, solids basis, and moisture are unknown; true NCO:OH after addition is unresolved; and all six major process-history fields are missing. The Planner explicitly states that unknown modifier functionality precludes interpreting loading percentage alone and that material stoichiometric changes require a matched control or reformulation.
critical_findings.issue: Reactive-equivalent and process uncertainties currently prevent clean interpretation of a performance result.

critical_findings.evidence: SI15-60 < 0.305 and SI15-90 < 0.550 are the numerical midpoints implied by being closer to the single measured E1 value than the single measured E5 value. They are labeled provisional, which avoids presenting them as literature facts, but their uncertainty basis, practical significance, and relation to a usable processing specification are not established.
critical_findings.issue: The proposed acceptance thresholds are reconstructed midpoint rules rather than locally validated performance boundaries.

critical_findings.evidence: The plan requires independent preparations and an uncertainty interval excluding E5 but gives no replicate count, interval definition, confidence level, variance model, or decision rule for the historically large E2 dispersion. E1 and E5 each have only one supplied hold run, so treating their point values as uncertainty-free references is not justified.
critical_findings.issue: The replicate and uncertainty requirements are not operationally specified.

critical_findings.evidence: The plan says to run S1C02 and, where feasible, E1 and E5. Given the E2 CV of approximately 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratio of approximately 2.8-3.6, S1C02 under the same process and hold schedule is essential rather than optional for distinguishing formulation effects from realization shifts.
critical_findings.issue: The contemporaneous reactive-core control is not mandatory in the measurement plan.

critical_findings.evidence: The shared-shape model is explicitly bounded to the original local chemistry family. The proposal plans to verify transfer on the first modified realization but does not specify an allowable shape or prediction error before later realizations are reduced to one-point calibration.
critical_findings.issue: Transfer of one-point state calibration to the modified chemistry lacks a frozen verification criterion.

interpretability_failures: A positive or negative S1C40 result cannot be assigned to the intended modifier intervention until AC1920 and TK100 reactive functionality, solids basis, moisture, and compatibility are verified and NCO:OH is recalculated.
A null result at 2.5 wt% TK100 would not distinguish failure of the tackifier-supported mitigation direction from use of a dose below the supplied evidence-supported region.
Without a mandatory contemporaneous replicated S1C02 control, candidate-control differences may be indistinguishable from the large E2 realization-state spread.
The phrase that absolute viscosity changes must show the same conclusion is not a quantitative acceptance rule.
No operational viscosity range defines what counts as retaining usable viscosity.
The state-anchor timing relative to the drifting 120 °C hold is insufficiently specified, so the anchor itself may depend on elapsed hold time.

leakage_check.detail: No held-out formulation identity or wet-lab outcome is visible, and the proposal explicitly disclaims their use. However, the payload states that the exact V2 grid and fine-refinement algorithm were formalized after the validation experiment, while S1C40 uses a 2.5 wt% tackifier refinement not present in the disclosed coarse 0/5/10 wt% hypothesis grid. Its provenance as a pre-result design choice is therefore not fully auditable.

regularity_alignment.detail: The proposal correctly targets the measured 120 °C time-dependent viscosity drift, separates starting viscosity from hold stability, incorporates realization-state controls, and avoids treating analogue distance as a performance prediction. However, S1C40 is promoted as a minimum-sufficient full-coverage intervention even though its 2.5 wt% tackifier loading is below the stated 3-10 wt% broad supported region and the directly documented 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster, while intervention sufficiency has not been established locally.

required_corrections: Verify and freeze AC1920 and TK100 solids content, OH value or other NCO-reactive functionality, moisture specification, compatibility information, and lot identity before selecting the performance formulation.
Recalculate true NCO:OH and mass balance after modifier addition; either preserve a specified reactive-equivalent basis or include a stoichiometrically matched control.

Do not describe 2.5 wt% TK100 as evidence-supported full coverage without an explicit conservative extrapolation rationale. Otherwise rerank to a full-coverage point whose individual axis doses lie within the supplied supported regions.
Do not invoke minimum sufficient intervention until sufficiency is supported; label S1C40 as a lower-dose uncertainty probe if it is retained.
Make replicated S1C02 under the identical preparation, state-anchor, sweep, and 120 °C hold schedule mandatory.

Specify the number of independent preparations, uncertainty-interval method and confidence level, handling of E1/E5 reference uncertainty, and the quantitative rule for deciding whether dispersion is comparable to historical E2 variability.
Define quantitative acceptance criteria for absolute viscosity change, usable initial viscosity, and thermal-response-shape transfer rather than relying on qualitative phrases.
Predefine anchor timing and the maximum allowable full-sweep shape or prediction error before one-point calibration is permitted for later realizations.
Document that the E1/E5 midpoint thresholds are conservative reconstructed decision rules, not directly measured pass limits or literature facts.
Resolve and document the provenance of the 2.5 wt% fine-grid level to show that it was not selected using the held-out validation formulation or result.

scientific_boundary_check.detail: The proposal generally respects the boundary between local measured drift and external analogue evidence, but rank-1 depends on calling a below-supported-region 2.5 wt% tackifier dose a full, strongly supported, minimum-sufficient intervention. That classification is not established by the supplied evidence, and unresolved stoichiometry and process history currently prevent an interpretable performance claim.

result.pattern: thermally stable reactive hot melt urethane composition

tool_trace.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: Required first bridge from the upstream physical analysis. It will establish whether formulation-only or state-aware description is supported, whether one-point state calibration is effective, and which temperature and hold responses must govern candidate selection.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, realization/process state primarily shifts viscosity scale while a low-complexity common thermal-response shape remains transferable.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.
